newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia civil servants said must vote for Golkar.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia civil servants said must vote for Golkar.

text.p: Indonesian Interior Minister Yogie Suardi Memet said the country's six million civil servants have no choice but to vote for the ruling Golkar party, the Jakarta Post newspaper reported on Friday.

"Legally, Korpri (Indonesian Civil Servants Corps) members are free to vote for any of the three political organisations," Memet told reporters after briefing provincial general election officials on Thursday.
"However, they are also bound to the statutes of Korpri and the results of its congress, which say that members must channel their political aspirations through Golkar," he added.
Indonesia has scheduled general elections for May 29.

The two minor parties, the Moslem-based United Development Party (PPP) and Christian-Nationalist Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI), have criticised Golkar's policy of urging civil servants to vote only for that party.

A recent survey by the state-sponsored Indonesian Institute of Sciences also has recommended that civil servants be allowed to join any political organisations. The survey suggested that public service standards would suffer if civil servants remain too closely tied to Golkar.
Memet, a member of Golkar and chairman of the election committee, has in the past suggested that civil servants should resign if they do not vote for Golkar.
Interior Ministry Secretary-General Suriatna Subrata was quoted by the Jakarta Post as denying that Golkar's policy had "castrated" the political rights of civil servants.

"The law guarantees that Korpri members can vote for any political grouping," he said. "But they would have to solicit their superiors' blessing before they could channel their aspirations through political groupings other than Golkar," he said. The paper gave no further details.
Although in theory Korpri is apolitical, the organisation is one of the main components of Golkar's election campaign machinery.
